Claude Opus 5.5 = your motion designer
How to create studio-quality motion from one prompt





Charlie Hills
Sep 27, 2026




40

2
4

Share





Three weeks ago I told you to move to Codex. I wrote a whole edition on it. Then a full beginner-to-advanced guide last Sunday. Two days later, Anthropic shipped Opus 5.5.
Anthropic had an absolute run at the start of the year. Everyone was obsessed, and I told a lot of you to switch (I used it for everything).
Then Opus dropped off. I moved to Codex and genuinely enjoyed it. The experience is really nice, and Astra was the best model around. Opus 5.5 changes that. It’s clearly the best again, and it feels like the good old days of Anthropic models.



That's roughly how the last five Opus releases have felt.
And I'll be honest. For two weeks I ran Astra on every single task (probably to my own detriment). My Codex account topped itself up 27 times this month. That's £2,044.28 in extra credit (ouch).



Those are two of the 27, both on the same day.
But Astra on every task was me paying top price for jobs that didn't need it. So I went back to Opus 5.5. It's 60% cheaper than Astra ($4 vs $10 per million input tokens).


It's cheaper than Opus 5 on every line, too.
And it does more with the money. On Anthropic’s chart, Opus 5.5 on medium beats Astra and Fable on their highest settings (for a fraction of the cost).


Top left is where you want to be. Opus 5.5 is orange, Astra is dark grey.
The output is exceptional too. It leads Astra and Fable on most of Anthropic’s tests (Astra still wins two).


Business workflows and science research are the two Astra keeps.
But the biggest jump is motion graphics. Opus 5.5 is a massive step up, and every video in this edition is the proof.
